grammar.label: mediating between two parties who disagree
grammar.form: restating each position in terms its holder accepts; naming the real disagreement
grammar.meaning: makes a dispute discussable by describing it neutrally

explanation.en: A mediator's first sentence is a test: each side must recognise itself in the description. That is harder than it sounds, because a neutral summary of a position usually sounds weaker to the person who holds it. Getting it right buys the standing to say what the actual disagreement is.
explanation.uz: Vositachining birinchi jumlasi — sinov: har ikki tomon o'zini tavsifda tanishi kerak. Bu ko'ringanidan qiyin, chunki neytral bayon egasiga zaifroq eshitiladi.

grammar.positive_example: You say the survey is out of date; you say it is the only one. Both are true.
grammar.negative_example: You are both making valid points and should try to find a compromise.

l1_notes.uz: Vositachilik tili neytral bo'lishi kerak, ammo neytral so'zlar ham baho tashiydi.

grammar.label: chairing — the grammar of controlling a discussion
grammar.form: the summarising intervention; the time-boxed invitation; the explicit close
grammar.meaning: moves a meeting forward without silencing anyone

explanation.en: A chair who says 'let me summarise' is not summarising; they are reclaiming the floor, and everyone knows it, and it is accepted because the summary that follows is useful. Chairing is a set of moves that are transparent and still work, which is unusual in language.
explanation.uz: 'Let me summarise' degan raisning maqsadi xulosa emas, so'zni qaytarib olish — buni hamma biladi va qabul qiladi, chunki keyingi xulosa foydali.

grammar.positive_example: Let me summarise where we are, and then I want to hear from the two who have not spoken.
grammar.negative_example: Let me summarise, and then perhaps we should all think about it a bit more.

l1_notes.uz: Yig'ilishni boshqarish shakllari ingliz professional muhitida standartlashgan.

body.speaker: Kamola
body.text: Those two have been arguing for forty minutes.

body.speaker: Kamola
body.text: Not any more. Listen to the last three exchanges.

body.speaker: Aziz
body.text: They are arguing about who was told first.

body.speaker: Kamola
body.text: Which is a different meeting, and neither of them has noticed. What do I say to bring them back?

body.speaker: Aziz
body.text: 'Both are true. The figures were late and the office was not told. Which do we fix first?'

body.speaker: Kamola
body.text: That is mediation. You accept both accounts and you make them choose an order.

body.speaker: Aziz
body.text: And if one of them is simply wrong?

body.speaker: Kamola
body.text: Then you say so, but not in that room and not in front of the other one.

body.speaker: Aziz
body.text: Bobur talks for nine minutes at a time.

body.speaker: Kamola
body.text: And a chair who lets him is not being kind to anybody. You say his name, you name the thing he said that was useful, and you give the floor to somebody else in the same breath.
